title: Runtime residency annotations and policy notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc collects notes and early decisions for an annotation-driven approach to data residency enforcement in Private deployments. Goal: allow per-request residency intent (hints/requirements) to travel with requests through the stack so the routing layer, cache layer, and enforcement hooks can make policy decisions without brittle config-only pinning.

Scope and motivation:
- Problem: customers want both coarse-grained region pinning (project-level) and fine-grained overrides for certain sensitive requests. Current model relies heavily on static model-region pin assignments which increases migration friction.
- Proposed direction: introduce runtime residency annotations + a small policy-evaluation layer in the control plane and runtime to make decisions at request time.

High-level model:
1) Residency annotation carriers:
   - HTTP header: X-Redwood-Residency: region=eu-west1;require=strict
   - SDK metadata: request.metadata.residency = {region: "eu-west1", level: "prefer"}
   - Service-to-service gRPC metadata for internal calls
2) Annotation semantics:
   - level=strict -> request must be satisfied by resources in specified region(s); fail closed
   - level=prefer -> prefer local region, fallback allowed after policy timeout (e.g., 150ms)
   - region=multi:eu -> allow any EU-certified region (eu-west1, eu-central1)
3) Where evaluated:
   - Edge ingress: quick accept/reject for strict mismatches (fast-path enforce)
   - Routing layer: choose pool based on region/latency/cost tradeoff
   - Cache layer: key derivation must include residency tag to avoid cross-region cache contamination
   - Serving runtime: ensure model variant chosen is certified for the region (quantized variants with different legal approvals)

Operator/implementation notes:
- Config: introduce residency profiles (name, allowedRegions, defaultLevel, escalationPolicy)
- Backwards compatibility: if no annotation present, fall back to project-level pinning config
- Cache key example: cache_key = sha256(model|route|user_tenant|residency_tag)
- Telemetry: emit residency_decision, chosen_region, fallback_reason, decision_latency

Testing and validation plan:
- Unit tests for policy evaluator (table-driven scenarios for strict/prefer/none)
- Synthetic load tests to measure decision latency at ingress (target <3ms p95)
- Chaos test: simulate region outage and verify fallback semantics (prefer -> fallback within policy timeout; strict -> 503)
- Migration test: convert 10 pilot customers to annotations and run A/B (10% traffic for 2 weeks)

Telemetry and SLOs to track:
- Percent of requests carrying residency annotation (baseline 0 -> target 50% during pilot)
- Residency decision latency p50/p95
- Strict-fail rate (should be ~0 for healthy config)
- Cross-region cache read percentage (should be low once annotations in place)

Security/legal considerations:
- Annotations are signaling only; enforcement must be auditable. All decisions must be logged with request id and policy id for legal audits.
- Signed annotations: for high-assurance customers, require signed residency tokens issued by control plane to prevent client spoofing. Format: residency_token=sig(base64)
- PII handling: communicate to Compliance that annotations do not change content handling; ensure KMS/HSM and audit logs used as before.

Migration strategy (pilot -> staged rollout):
- Phase 1 (pilot): opt-in customers, SDK update with annotation helper, collect telemetry, no strict enforcement (prefer only)
- Phase 2 (early adoption): enable strict for test workloads behind canary routing, policy UI to map project to allowedRegions
- Phase 3 (general availability): enable signed-residency tokens for enterprise, add enforcement to edge layer, update runbooks

Operator runbook snippets (quick reference):
- To debug a stuck request: check request headers for residency, look up policy id in control plane, inspect routing trace (trace tags: residency.decide, residency.pool), verify model variant compatibility
- Emergency rollback: add 'residency.allow_fallback=true' to control plane policy to restore traffic during regional maintenance

Open questions / TODOs:
- Policy expression language: do we reuse existing routing policy DSL or define a minimal residency-specific grammar? @Marco to propose by 2025-03-25
- Rollout UX: how does Console expose per-route residency overrides without confusing users? mockups needed. @Evelyn
- Billing implications: when a prefer fallback crosses billing regions, how to surface cost impact to customers? Product + Finance input required

Related artifacts and tickets:
- RES-412: residency annotation PoC
- Confluence: Runtime Residency Design (link above)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic: prefer a narrow, well-instrumented feature that can be expanded. Focus of this doc is the runtime/telemetry implications rather than full legal matrix.
- Please add comments inline in the doc, and flag any legal constraints we missed.

Checklist before merging to design RFC:
- [ ] Policy evaluator tests
- [ ] Ingress fast-path prototype
- [ ] Cache key change landed with compatibility flag
- [ ] Telemetry dashboard skeleton
- [ ] Legal sign-off on signed tokens

End of notes.
